corrections.evidence: Runtime catalog crawl is API-FIRST: catalog-crawler.ts:280 calls adapter.fetchCatalogPage when it exists (WooCommerce implements it), passing perPage=profilePerPage(100) (line 268,290). woocommerce.ts:299 caps Math.min(perPage??100,100)=100 and walks /wp-json/wp/v2/product (line 346). HTML pagination (and the broken template) only fire when fetchCatalogPage returns null OR after 3 empty API cycles (catalog-crawler.ts:343-362).

corrections.evidence: 2149 unique IDs from the SINGLE global endpoint /wp-json/wp/v2/product (overlap-free). corrections.round1Hypothesis: candidate hasWaf=false (cloudflare-passive, rapid-burst untested by design). DB hasWaf=true wordfence-on-cloudflare-passive rateLimit410After=7 (burst).
corrections.liveMethod: Sustained spaced walk (24 sequential requests at 1.2s: 2 count probes + 22 API pages) + header inspection. NOTE: the no-delay burst was intentionally NOT run — it was blocked by the safety classifier as a violation of the user's explicit >=1s spacing boundary, and I did not work around it.
corrections.evidence: ZERO 410/429/403 across 24 sequential requests at 1.2s spacing — Wordfence does not fire at >=1s cadence. Headers on normal 200: Server: cloudflare, CF-RAY present, cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC, NO Wordfence response headers (Wordfence only surfaces on a block). DB's rateLimit410After=7 was measured on an UNSPACED burst (2026-04-11) — that risk is real only without spacing. Production crawler runs at >=2s gaps (Phase-0 budget). THEME-D over-throttle cost is LIMITED here: catalog-crawler.ts:290 perPage=profilePerPage(100) WINS over the hasWaf?20 default, and woocommerce.ts:299 caps at 100 regardless — so hasWaf:true does NOT throttle perPage on this site (unlike intersurplus where perPage was unset). The only hasWaf:true cost is slightly more conservative delays + empty-page tolerance (catalog-crawler.ts:306-316).
corrections.proposedValue: Keep hasWaf=true + wafType='wordfence-on-cloudflare-passive' (DB is JUSTIFIED, not over-set): a real Wordfence rate-limit exists on bursts (410 after ~7 unspaced). It is non-blocking at the crawler's >=1s/>=2s cadence. This is the correct posture for a site that bans on bursts — candidate's hasWaf=false would be UNSAFE if any future code path bursts. Recommend documenting rateLimit410After=7 + 'safe at >=1s spacing'.

corrections.field: watermark date filter field (after vs modified_after)
corrections.liveMethod: Live test of both params on /wp-json/wp/v2/product (7-day cutoff) + CODE TRACE of the actual runtime mapping (watermark-crawler.ts:207-211 + woocommerce.ts:339-344).
corrections.evidence: Live: after=<7d> -> x-wp-total=3 (newly PUBLISHED); modified_after=<7d> -> x-wp-total=55 (created-or-edited); after=2030 -> 0 (filter honored, not ignored). CODE: watermark-crawler.ts passes options.dateAfter to the adapter and does NOT read apiDateFilterField from the profile. woocommerce.ts:343 hardcodes options.dateAfter -> params.modified_after and line 339 uses orderby='modified' when a date filter is present. So the RUNTIME always uses modified_after + orderby=modified regardless of the profile field. Therefore the DB's apiDateFilterField:'after' is NOT honored by code; the candidate's 'modified_after' matches actual runtime behavior. Design intent (woocommerce.ts:332 comment): catch restocks/price-changes, not just new publishes.
corrections.proposedValue: watermark.dateFilterField = 'modified_after' (matches the adapter-hardcoded runtime). Flag: the *DateFilterField profile field is currently DEAD (adapter ignores it and always sends modified_after). Either wire the adapter to read it, or drop the field from the profile schema.

codeFindings.detail: buildPaginatedUrl type:'path' strips base trailing slash (line 124) then appends template raw (line 125). DB template 'page/{N}/' (no leading slash) => base '.../firearms/' -> '.../firearms' + 'page/2/' = '.../firearmspage/2/' (404). The bug is REAL. HOWEVER it is INERT on dantesports because the runtime catalog path is API-first (catalog-crawler.ts:280, woocommerce.ts:294) and buildPaginatedUrl (lines 781/957/996) only runs on the HTML fallback (catalog-crawler.ts:362, !apiCrawlUsed). It would only bite if the WC API path failed AND HTML fallback engaged. Fix recommendation stands (defensive leading-slash normalization in buildPaginatedUrl), but it is not a live coverage blocker here.

Candidate's object form {wp-rest-header,...} is valid + live-verified (x-wp-total=2149).

Runtime is API-first via adapter.fetchCatalogPage; perPage=profilePerPage(DB 100) (line 268,290); WC adapter caps Math.min(perPage??100,100)=100 (woocommerce.ts:299) walking /wp-json/wp/v2/product (line 346). The literal 'api-full-catalog' string is NEVER read (0 grep hits) — dispatch is presence-of-fetchCatalogPage, not the profile method string. DB perPage=100 is the consumed field; candidate perPage=12 is the inert HTML render floor.

So neither DB's 'after' nor any profile value is honored; runtime is always modified_after+orderby=modified. Candidate's 'modified_after' matches runtime; DB's 'after' is aspirational/dead.
